entries.objective: To compare CBS with related aperiodic server approaches (PS, DS, SS, TBS) and identify the key differences in scheduling base, formal guarantees, and overload behavior.
entries.prompt: Compare Constant Bandwidth Server with Polling Server, Deferrable Server, Sporadic Server, and Total Bandwidth Server. Analyze differences in scheduler base, schedulability guarantee, overload behavior, and budget rules.
entries.ai_output_summary: Claude produced a structured comparison table and detailed analysis of CBS vs PS, DS, SS, and TBS covering scheduling framework, formal schedulability guarantees, overload handling, and budget replenishment rules.

actions: Compared Claude output against Abeni 1998 (RTSS proceedings pp. 4-13) and Abeni 2004 (Real-Time Systems vol. 27 no. 2 pp. 123-167). Cross-checked TBS deadline assignment formula. Verified DS schedulability violation claim against Buttazzo primary reference.

issues: Formal details verified against Abeni 1998 and Abeni 2004 papers. TBS deadline assignment formula cross-checked.

integration.section: Section 9 - Comparison of Aperiodic Server Approaches

entries.reflection: This interaction helped structure the comparison between CBS and neighboring servers. The output was partially accepted - the table structure was used but all technical claims were verified against primary sources before inclusion.

entries.objective: To identify and analyze engineering tradeoffs between CBS and related approaches including precision vs simplicity, isolation vs efficiency, and single-core vs multi-core constraints.
entries.prompt: Analyze the engineering tradeoffs of Constant Bandwidth Server compared to TBS, DS, and SS. Cover precision vs simplicity, formal guarantee vs deployability, isolation strength vs utilization efficiency, and single-core vs multi-core limitations.
entries.ai_output_summary: Claude produced a structured tradeoff analysis covering five dimensions: precision vs simplicity, formal guarantee vs practical deployability, isolation strength vs utilization efficiency, single-core vs multi-core, and offline vs online parameter selection.

actions: Tradeoff claims cross-checked against Abeni 2004 and Buttazzo primary reference. EDF deployability constraint verified against known RTOS literature. Multi-core limitation confirmed as out of scope in original CBS formulation.

issues: Multi-core discussion was generalized. Adaptive CBS variants mentioned but not deeply analyzed as they are outside basic CBS scope.

entries.reflection: This interaction helped identify the key tradeoffs of CBS in embedded systems contexts. Output was partially accepted - structure was used but claims were verified and rewritten in my own words.

entries.objective: To identify concrete embedded systems deployment scenarios where CBS is suitable and unsuitable, and analyze the OS support requirements for CBS implementation.
entries.prompt: Identify practical embedded systems scenarios where Constant Bandwidth Server is suitable and unsuitable. Include OS support requirements, memory and energy considerations, and concrete deployment examples.
entries.ai_output_summary: Claude identified suitable deployment example (robotic controller with periodic sensor fusion plus event-driven network handlers) and unsuitable example (legacy automotive ECU with AUTOSAR fixed-priority OS). Also covered POSIX SCHED_DEADLINE as a CBS-like Linux implementation, memory overhead, and energy considerations under DVFS.

actions: POSIX SCHED_DEADLINE reference verified as a known CBS-based implementation in Linux kernel. AUTOSAR fixed-priority constraint verified against known embedded OS literature. Memory and energy claims checked for plausibility against CBS formal definition.

issues: POSIX SCHED_DEADLINE details were not deeply analyzed. Energy analysis under DVFS was generalized and not formally proven.

entries.reflection: This interaction helped identify concrete deployment contexts for CBS. The suitable and unsuitable examples were useful starting points but were rewritten and verified before inclusion in the milestone document.
